title: Dispute resolution method
description: content/methods/<id>.yaml: one way of resolving or handling a dispute, from any tradition. The list of methods is open: a process nobody has recorded yet is added as a new record with status 'proposed', with no change to any schema. Other records refer to methods by id in a 'methods' list. A method is described by what it is called, where it comes from and how it works (its characteristics), so a process that fits no existing name can still be recorded and compared. See docs/decisions/0012-open-list-of-dispute-resolution-methods.md.

id.description: Stable identifier used in 'methods' lists. Must match the file name. Never reused.

name.description: The name the project uses in English prose, e.g. 'mediation', 'early neutral evaluation'.

names_in_language.description: Names the process has in the language of the people who practice it, as they or the cited source write it, with every diacritic kept.

romanized.description: A romanized form, when the source gives one.

also_known_as.description: Other English names and spellings, e.g. 'ombudsman' for ombuds.

classification.description: How the project classifies the method. alternative-dispute-resolution: a process the sources treat as ADR. own-tradition: a practice of a people or community that the project does not file under ADR, such as peacemaking or customary processes (charter, commitment 3). court-process: a step inside litigation, such as a settlement conference, that sources also discuss with ADR. governmental-process: a process of government decision making, such as negotiated rulemaking. unsettled: sources disagree or the project has not decided; say why in 'classification_note'. other: none of these; say why.

classification_note.description: Markdown. Required when classification is 'unsettled' or 'other'; otherwise optional.

tradition.description: Where the method comes from. More than one may apply.

definition.description: Markdown. Cites sources with [@key] and labels the project's own analysis.

characteristics.description: How the method works, recorded as facets so that any process, including one not seen before, can be described and compared. Every facet is a list, allows 'varies' and 'other', and is explained in 'note' when the short values do not fit.

note.description: Markdown. Anything the facets cannot say, with citations.

broader.description: Ids of methods this one is a kind of, e.g. evaluative mediation is a kind of mediation. Never used to place an own-tradition method under an ADR method.

combines.description: For hybrid processes: the ids of the methods it combines, in order, e.g. mediation then arbitration.

jurisdictions.description: Where the method is documented in law or practice, when that matters to its definition (for example a process established by one territory's statute).

tribes.description: Tribe profile ids, for a process particular to one or more nations. Such a record follows the charter's consultation process.

glossary.description: Id of the glossary entry for this term, if text links to it with [[id]].

sources.description: Keys of source records relied on for the definition and characteristics.

status.description: proposed: recorded but not yet reviewed by the lead author. adopted: reviewed. retired: replaced; see redirect_to.
